messages:

Subject: Tenant evacuation and data retention cutover questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Monday. We're mapping out an internal runbook for moving our tenant off of Redwood Dedicated in the event of a jurisdictional decommission. A few specific questions we need answered for our legal & infosec signoff:

- If we request a tenant evacuation (region unpin + decommission), what exact steps happen to our persisted state (snapshots, backups, and any async replicas)?
- How long after we mark the tenant for deletion will any recoverable snapshot remain? Is there a tombstone window?
- Does Redwood rotate or rekey KMS material as part of the purge flow?
- We need an auditable proof-of-delete (log entries + snapshot manifest). Can we get an example artifact?

Really appreciate concise, actionable answers — our deadline for the security review is next Thursday.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Head of IT Security
ClearRiver Financial

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: security@clearriver.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant evacuation and data retention cutover questions

Hi Sophie — thanks, clear list. I put together a short checklist and an answers summary attached (tenant-evacuation-checklist.xlsx, retention-cutover-summary.pdf). Highlights below so you can copy into your runbook:

1) Sequence on tenant evacuation (high level)
   - Request received & validated by Redwood: we create an evacuation ticket and schedule a drain window (you pick a 2–8 hour SLA window).
   - Live request routing: active traffic is drained from the tenant, existing KV caches are flushed to ephemeral store, ongoing requests routed to fallback model variant.
   - Snapshot and immutable export: system triggers a point-in-time snapshot export to object storage in the region pinned by the tenant; manifest stored in our audit service.
   - Replica sweep: asynchronous replicas (if any) are queued for deletion; we mark them as 'scheduled for purge' and begin propagation to delete workers.
   - Tombstone period: by default we keep snapshot manifests and on-object storage blobs for 30 days post-request unless you request immediate purge; during that period we can restore from the snapshot.
   - Final purge: after the tombstone window (or immediately if you request immediate purge and sign the waiver), data blobs are cryptographically deleted and references removed from metadata indexes.

2) KMS / keying
   - We do not rekey customer data automatically during standard evacuation. If you request immediate cryptographic destruction, we can perform a KMS key rotation + key destruction step as part of the purge (requires approval and takes ~1–2 hours). We'll give you an HSM-backed key rotation record for your audit.

3) Proofs / artifacts
   - We provide: (a) snapshot manifest (hashes + object paths); (b) purge job IDs with timestamps; (c) audit log excerpts showing job execution and operator IDs; (d) checksum verification report. Example artifacts are in the attached PDF.

4) Retention and custom tombstone windows
   - Default tombstone: 30 days.
   - Options: 0 days (immediate purge), 7, 14, 30, 90 available. Immediate purge requires a signed acceptance and will disable restore options.

If you want, we can run a dry-run evacuation on a non-prod tenant to produce sample artifacts for your reviewers. Let me know your preferred tombstone window and whether you want KMS destruction included.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tenant-evacuation-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), retention-cutover-summary.pdf (PDF)

Team — forwarding ClearRiver request. They want a dry-run on TG-qa-001 with a 7-day tombstone, no KMS rotation. Please confirm the following and any ops caveats:

- Are cross-region archive copies included in the manifest we hand to customers, or do we flag them separately? (Sophie asks).

- Expected timelines: drain window + snapshot export should complete within the selected 4 hour window; replica sweep completed within 24 hours; manifest + audit excerpt available within 1 hour of snapshot completion. Anything likely to push that?

I've attached an ops-redline doc with where I think the gaps are. Please reply-all with one-line confirmations so I can pass to Sophie.

Thanks,
Tessa

Tessa / team — confirmations: 

- Cross-region archival copies: treated as separate replica objects; manifests include a pointer to archival sets but we mark the objects as 'archival-replica' so customers can see location + retention policy.
- Artifacts location: snapshot manifest + audit excerpt will be uploaded to the customer's S3 bucket via pre-signed URL (we also publish a Drive backup for internal review).
- Audit JSON schema: operator_id, job_id, job_start_ts, job_end_ts, object_paths[], object_hashes[], action_type, run_status — we can produce a sample; I'll attach one to the ticket.
- Timelines: drain + snapshot export in the 4-hour SLA is realistic for TG-qa-001. Replica sweep for non-prod usually completes <6 hours; production could be up to 24 hours depending on snapshot size. Manifest + audit excerpt available within 1 hour after snapshot finalization.

I'll create the dry-run ticket (OP-DR-4642) and share presigned link + sample JSON.

-Vanessa

Signature: Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
